structure: Part 1 of 16 of repos/trade-imports-ins-tests (HEAD c293b056f39efb206c6c4f2df54c38e5febd8485): the eight per-page end-to-end specs for the live-animals journey's data-entry pages, read in full with every page object, domain constant, flow, fixture and config file the partition's `read` names. The specs are tests/animals/e2e/pages/{origin,import-reason,consignment-details,arrival-details,commodities,animal-identification,cph-number,additional-details}.spec.ts plus that folder's README.md. Each spec is one or more test.describe blocks, every one tagged @duplicated-in-frontend, reaching its page only through an AnimalsJourney `to*` method (flows/animals/journey.ts) handed to it by the ui fixture, and asserting through a page object under page-objects/animals/ against copy and option lists held in domain/animals/constants/. Several describes repeat the whole block with test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false }) to prove the page works without JavaScript. Literal test() declarations: origin 26, import-reason 8, consignment-details 11, arrival-details 13, commodities 17, animal-identification 13, cph-number 7, additional-details 3, which is 98 tests, two of them generated by a loop over a table of cases (origin's region-code storage pair and its one-entry setUps table), so 99 at run time. Covered here: the eight pages' routes under /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/, their headings and captions, every field with its label, hint, options and legend, every validation message the specs prove verbatim, the conditional reveals (the origin region-code panel and its JavaScript prefix, the purpose and exit questions behind each import reason, the identifier cards each commodity choice reveals), what each page's Save and continue and Save and return to overview are proven to do and where each lands, the Back link's two destinations on origin, the selected-commodities summary table, the type-ahead and MOJ date-picker components these pages use, and the seeded form field names the same pages accept. Not covered here: the addresses, transited-countries and transporter pages (part 2), and the review, declaration, confirmation, notification view and notification list pages (part 3). Nine gap claims record where the slice is silent on something its pages plainly have, including the type-ahead announcements the part's own scope names.

claims.statement: Every live-animals question page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference number>/<page slug>.
claims.note: setBase for these pages is SET_BASES.liveAnimals, '/live-animals'.

claims.statement: A trader starts a new live-animals notification from the notification dashboard's Create new notification button and lands on the Origin of the import page, which already carries the new notification's reference number in its address.
A live-animals notification's reference number reads GBN-AG, a two-digit number and six upper-case letters or digits, joined by hyphens.

Save and continue walks the live-animals journey in this order: main import reason, commodity details, identification details, additional details, arrival details, transit countries, transport details, upload documents, consignment addresses, contact address.
claims.quote:
const stops: SaveAndContinueStop[] = [
      this.animalsPages.importReason,
      this.animalsPages.consignmentDetails,
      this.animalsPages.animalIdentification,
      this.animalsPages.additionalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.arrivalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.transitedCountries,
      this.animalsPages.transporter,
      this.animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments,
      this.animalsPages.addresses,
      this.animalsPages.contactAddress,
    ];

claims.statement: An air or sea consignment's overview task list holds eleven rows in this order: Where is this consignment coming from?, What are you importing?, Main import reason, Commodity details, Identification details, Additional details, Arrival details, Transport details, Upload documents, Consignment addresses, Contact address for this consignment.
claims.quote:
export const AIR_OR_SEA_OVERVIEW_TASKS = [
  'Where is this consignment coming from?',
  'What are you importing?',
  IMPORT_REASON_TASK,
  'Commodity details',
  'Identification details',
  'Additional details',
  'Arrival details',
  'Transport details',
  'Upload documents',
  CONSIGNMENT_ADDRESSES,
  'Contact address for this consignment',
] as const;

claims.statement: An overland consignment's overview task list holds a twelfth row, Transit countries, between Arrival details and Transport details.
Each live-animals question page offers a button labelled exactly Save and continue.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save and continue', exact: true });

claims.statement: Each live-animals question page offers a second button labelled exactly Save and return to overview.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save and return to overview', exact: true });

claims.statement: A live-animals question page carries a link labelled exactly Back.
A live-animals question page carries a journey strip holding the notification's status tag and its reference number.
The overview task list shows each task's state as text, Complete when it is answered and To do when it is not.
A refused page shows an error summary headed There is a problem.
claims.quote: await expect(pages.page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'There is a problem' })).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: A refused page's browser tab title starts with Error: .
A search box on these pages is an accessible autocomplete that enhances a native select of the same name, so without JavaScript the trader uses the plain select instead.
claims.quote: /** A type-ahead that enhances a native select, addressed by the select's id. */

claims.statement: An accessible autocomplete on these pages announces how many results are available, in the form "3 results are available." or "1 result is available.", and announces a highlighted option as "<option> 1 of 3 is highlighted".
claims.note: No spec in this part asserts these announcements; the helper is used by specs in other parts.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts the country or port search's announcements, its search-button styling or its hint on the origin page, although the part's own scope names them.
claims.note: Looked for expectResultCountAnnounced, expectFirstOptionAnnounced, expectSearchButtonStyledAsGovukBlue, typeAhead.hint and typeAhead.announcement in all eight specs: none appears.

claims.statement: A date field on these pages uses the Ministry of Justice date picker, which carries data-min-date and data-max-date bounds the page serves and a Choose date button opening a dialog.
A date typed into one of these pages is entered as dd/mm/yyyy, and a date the service shows back in a hint or message reads d/m/yyyy.
The notification journey's pages are reached by walking them, never by seeding, and a page test asserts one page's rendering, interaction and validation and nothing beyond it.
claims.quote: - A page test focuses on validating a single page’s behaviour (rendering, interaction, and validation) and stays within that page’s scope.

claims.statement: The Origin of the import page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/origin.
The origin page is headed, at level one, Origin of the import.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Origin of the import' });

claims.statement: The origin page asks for a country of origin through a search box over a select named countryOfOrigin.
The origin page asks "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?" as a group of Yes and No radios.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('group', { name: 'Does the consignment have a region of origin code?' });

claims.statement: The region of origin question is described by the hint "Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now."
claims.quote: 'Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.'

claims.statement: Answering Yes to the region of origin question reveals a box labelled Enter the region of origin code.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByLabel('Enter the region of origin code', { exact: true });

claims.statement: The region of origin code box is described by the hint Enter up to 5 characters.
The origin page offers an optional box labelled "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)".
claims.quote: return this.page.getByLabel('Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)');

claims.statement: The internal reference box is described by the hint "Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank."
claims.quote: const INTERNAL_REFERENCE_HINT = 'Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.';

claims.statement: The origin page's form holds Save and continue as its only button and no link at all.
claims.note: The origin page therefore offers no Save and return to overview and no cancel link, unlike the later question pages.

claims.statement: Back on the origin page returns the trader to the notification dashboard when the page was opened from the dashboard.
claims.quote: test('Back returns to the dashboard when the page was opened from the dashboard'

claims.statement: Back on the origin page returns the trader to that notification's overview, at the overview's own address, when the page was opened from the overview after origin answers were saved.
The region of origin code box stops accepting typing at five characters, and has autocomplete off and spellcheck false.
Save and continue with a country of origin chosen and No to the region of origin question takes the trader to the commodity selection page.
Save and continue with no country chosen holds the trader on the origin page and shows Select a country of origin in the error summary and against the country field.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.originOfImport.errorSummary).toContainText('Select a country of origin');
    await expect(animalsPages.originOfImport.country.error).toContainText('Select a country of origin');

claims.statement: A refused origin page shows the country search empty and keeps the internal reference the trader typed.
Answering Yes to the region of origin question and leaving the code box empty is refused with an error summary.
claims.quote: test('shows an error summary when a region of origin code is claimed but not given'

claims.statement: A saved region of origin code is shown back on the origin page with Yes still selected.
Changing the region of origin answer to No clears the saved code: the notification then shows its region of origin code as Not applicable, and choosing Yes again opens an empty box.
A territory may be chosen as the country of origin: it is saved, shown back named with its country, such as Canary Islands (Spain), and its country's code, ES, is shown as the region code prefix.
claims.note: The display 'Canary Islands (Spain)' comes from subdivisionByCode in resources/reference-data/reference-data.ts:39-47, which names a subdivision '<subdivision> (<country>)'.

claims.statement: With JavaScript, the region code box carries a prefix that is shown but empty before a country of origin is chosen.
With JavaScript, choosing a country of origin puts that country's code into the region code prefix at once, and choosing another replaces it, without leaving the page.
With JavaScript, choosing a territory puts its country's code into the region code prefix without saving the page.
With JavaScript, clearing the chosen country of origin empties the region code prefix.
A refused origin page shows the country code the trader submitted as the region code prefix, and changes it when another country is chosen.
claims.quote: test('shows the submitted country code as the region code prefix on a refused page'

claims.statement: An origin page shown again after a save shows the saved country's code as the region code prefix beside the saved region code, and changes the prefix when another country is chosen, without leaving the page.
The region code prefix is hidden from screen readers.
The region code box is named to a screen reader by its label and described by its hint.
Without JavaScript the region code prefix is still in the page but hidden, on a first view, on a page shown again after a save, and on a refused page.
A region of origin code is stored with its country's code in front of it: typing 75 against France stores FR-75, and typing FR-75 stores FR-75 as well.
claims.quote: test(`stores a region code typed as ${typed} as ${FRANCE_REGION_CODE}`
claims.note: This is the one looped table in the part: two cases, 75 and FR-75.

claims.statement: A region of origin code longer than five characters after the country code is refused with the message Region of origin code must be 5 characters or less, even when the box's own length limit is removed.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Region of origin code must be 5 characters or less' });

claims.statement: The default region of origin code the suite answers with is 75.
The origin page's country search shows Select a country in its empty state and Search for a country as its placeholder.
claims.quote:
export const ORIGIN_COUNTRY_SELECT_TEXT = 'Select a country';
export const ORIGIN_COUNTRY_SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER = 'Search for a country';
claims.note: No spec in this part asserts either value; they are asserted by specs in other parts.

claims.statement: The country of origin list the suite answers from holds the EU and EEA countries, Switzerland and the United Kingdom's near neighbours by name, and country subdivisions such as ES-CN.
claims.note: mechanism: resolves each code against the captured origin-country fixture rather than naming the display text; the display comes from reference-data, so this is evidence of which codes the suite uses, not of the list MDM serves.

claims.statement: The origin page accepts the answers countryOfOrigin, regionOfOriginCodeRequirement, regionOfOriginCodeSuffix and internalReferenceNumber when posted straight to it.
claims.quote:
countryOfOrigin: answers.countryCode.value,
    regionOfOriginCodeRequirement: answers.requiresRegionCode.toLowerCase(),
    regionOfOriginCodeSuffix: answers.regionCode ?? '',
claims.note: mechanism: builds the origin page's form body from a notification's answers; shows the field names and that the region code is posted as a suffix, the prefix being the country's own code.

claims.statement: The Main import reason page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/import-reason.
The import reason page is headed, at level one and as its only main heading, Main import reason, and its browser tab reads Main import reason - Import notification service - GOV.UK.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.importReason.mainHeadings).toHaveText(['Main import reason']);
    await expect(pages.page).toHaveTitle('Main import reason - Import notification service - GOV.UK');

claims.statement: The import reason page asks "What is the main reason for importing the animals?" as one group of radios.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('group', { name: 'What is the main reason for importing the animals?' });

claims.statement: The main import reason offers at least these choices: Internal market, Re-entry, Transhipment or onward travel, Transit and Temporary admission horses.
claims.note: Each of the five is checked or asserted visible by a test; the specs never assert the whole option list, so a sixth choice would go unnoticed.

claims.statement: No main import reason is selected when the page opens.
Choosing Re-entry and pressing Save and return to overview is accepted and takes the trader to the overview.
Choosing Internal market reveals a purpose question whose options include Breeding, with none of them selected, and choosing one is accepted.
The internal market purpose offers Breeding and Companion animal not for resale or rehoming.
Choosing Internal market and leaving the purpose unanswered is refused with the error Select a purpose in the internal market, and the trader stays on the import reason page.
claims.quote:
await expect(pages.page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Select a purpose in the internal market' })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(animalsPages.importReason.heading).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: Choosing Transhipment or onward travel reveals a destination country search, Transit reveals both a port of exit search and a destination country search, and Temporary admission horses reveals a port of exit search.
Every destination country and port of exit search on the import reason page shows Select one in its empty box.
Without JavaScript every destination country and port of exit on the import reason page is a plain select whose first option reads Select one.
A transhipment destination country list offers territories as well as countries, their option values holding a hyphen.
claims.note: Read from the page object's territory locator, which selects options whose value contains a hyphen, the shape of a subdivision code such as ES-CN. No spec in this part asserts it.

claims.statement: Choosing Temporary admission horses also asks for an exit date, entered in a Ministry of Justice date picker on the field temporaryAdmissionExitDate.
claims.note: No spec in this part asserts the exit date's label, hint or validation; the journey only fills it.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts the temporary-admission exit date's label, hint or validation, nor any error for a transit or transhipment answer left blank.
claims.note: The spec's only validation test is the internal market purpose; the transit, transhipment and temporary admission branches are only checked for their reveals and placeholders.

claims.statement: The three main import reasons the suite answers with are internalMarket, transit and temporaryAdmissionHorses, shown as Internal market, Transit and Temporary admission horses.
The import reason page accepts the answers reasonForImport and purposeInInternalMarket when posted straight to it, and both may be left out.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the import reason page's form body; shows the field names and that a seeded draft can be left with the main import reason unanswered.

claims.statement: Main import reason is also the name of the overview's task row for this page.
The Commodity details page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/consignment-details.
The Commodity details page is headed, at level one, Commodity details, directly under the caption Description of the goods.
The Commodity details page asks for a Number of animals and a Number of packages (when required) for each species chosen.
The Commodity details page lists the chosen commodities in a table named Selected commodities whose columns are Commodity code, Species and Actions.
A Selected commodities row shows the commodity code, the species label and a Remove control named Remove followed by the code and the species label.
A species is labelled by its Latin name and then its common name in brackets, such as Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle), and by its Latin name alone when it has no common name.
claims.quote:
export const speciesLabel = (species: SpeciesNamePair): string =>
  species.commonName ? `${species.latinName} (${species.commonName})` : species.latinName;

claims.statement: The number of animals box is empty when the Commodity details page opens.
A number of animals and a number of packages given together are accepted, and Save and return to overview takes the trader to the overview.
A number of animals above 2,147,483,647 is refused with the message Number of animals must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer, and the digits typed are kept on the page.
claims.quote: name: 'Number of animals must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer',

claims.statement: A number of animals of exactly 2,147,483,647 is saved and shown back on the page when it is reopened from the overview's Commodity details task.
A missing number of animals is refused with Enter the number of animals, and a number of packages that is not a whole number with Number of packages must be a whole number, like 5.
The error summary lists every number of animals error before any number of packages error, and each link moves focus to the box it names.
When one commodity code covers two chosen species, the Selected commodities table shows one row for the code with both species labels one per line, in alphabetical order.
Removing one commodity from the Commodity details page keeps the number of animals already typed for the species that is left, and the table drops to that one row.

The Commodity details page offers a link Add another commodity, which opens the commodity selection page; adding a species there and saving returns to Commodity details with the counts already saved still filled in and the new species' boxes empty.
The Commodity details page accepts the answers numberOfAnimalsQuantity-<line index> and numberOfPackages-<line index> when posted straight to it, one pair per commodity line.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the Commodity details page's form body from the notification's commodity lines, indexed by the line's position.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts the Number of packages (when required) hint or its upper limit, nor any error for a number of animals of zero or a negative number.
claims.note: The only packages rule proven is that it must be a whole number; the only animals limit proven is the upper bound.

claims.statement: The Arrival details page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/port-of-entry.
The Arrival details page is headed, at level one, Arrival details.
The Arrival details page asks for a port of entry, an arrival date, a means of transport to the port of entry, a transport identification and a transport document reference.
The arrival date is hinted "The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. For example, 27/3/2026", a fixed example rather than a date that moves with today.
claims.quote: 'The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. For example, 27/3/2026',

claims.statement: The port of entry search is hinted "Select where the transporter will enter with the consignment. Start typing to search by port or airport name or code."
claims.quote: 'Select where the transporter will enter with the consignment. Start typing to search by port or airport name or code.',

claims.statement: The port of entry search opens empty, shows Select a port as its placeholder, and the select behind it offers Select a port as its empty option.
claims.quote:
export const PORT_OF_ENTRY_SELECT_TEXT = 'Select a port';
export const PORT_OF_ENTRY_SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER = 'Select a port';

claims.statement: A port is shown as its name then a hyphen then its code, such as Aberdeen Harbour - GB ABD.
claims.note: The port list the suite answers from holds airports, seaports and rail ports, each with a code, a name and a type.

claims.statement: The means of transport to the port of entry offers, in this order, Select one, Air, Rail, Road and Sea.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.arrivalDetails.meansOfTransportOptions).toHaveText([
      MEANS_OF_TRANSPORT_SELECT_TEXT,
      meansOfTransport.airplane.display,
      meansOfTransport.railway.display,
      meansOfTransport.roadVehicle.display,
      meansOfTransport.vessel.display,
    ]);
claims.note: The values behind the four labels are AIRPLANE, RAILWAY, ROAD_VEHICLE and VESSEL.

claims.statement: The means of transport is a plain select, not a search box.

The transport identification hint opens "Enter one of the following:" and lists flight number, train number, road vehicle registration number, and vessel name (for ferries, also the road vehicle registration number).
The port of entry and the means of transport are both unanswered when the Arrival details page opens.
A full set of arrival answers saved with Save and return to overview marks the overview's Arrival details task Complete.

Save and continue with no means of transport is refused with Select a means of transport to the port of entry, shown in the error summary and against the select, which is marked with the GOV.UK error style, and the summary link moves focus to the select.
claims.quote: export const MEANS_OF_TRANSPORT_REQUIRED_MESSAGE = 'Select a means of transport to the port of entry';

claims.statement: A refused Arrival details page shows the port and arrival date the trader gave back on the page but saves neither: reopening the task from the overview shows both empty.

A means of transport may be saved on its own, with the other arrival answers left blank; the overview's Arrival details task then reads To do, and reopening the page shows no error summary, the saved means of transport and every other box empty.
The arrival date picker is restricted to one week before today and six months after it.

An arrival date typed outside that window is refused with Arrival date at port of entry must be between <earliest> and <latest>, naming both bounds as d/m/yyyy dates, and the trader stays on the Arrival details page.
claims.quote: const OUT_OF_RANGE_MESSAGE = `Arrival date at port of entry must be between ${EARLIEST_ALLOWED} and ${LATEST_ALLOWED}`;

claims.statement: An arrival date outside the allowed window is not saved: reopening the task shows the arrival date empty.
The Arrival details page accepts the answers arrivalDateAtPort, portOfEntry, meansOfTransport, transportIdentification and transportDocumentReference when posted straight to it.
claims.quote:
arrivalDateAtPort: answers.arrivalDate,
    portOfEntry: answers.pointOfEntry.value,
    meansOfTransport: answers.meansOfTransport.value,
    transportIdentification: answers.transportIdentification,
    transportDocumentReference: answers.transportDocumentReference,
claims.note: mechanism: builds the Arrival details page's form body from the notification's answers; its slug is port-of-entry.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts an error for a missing port of entry, a missing arrival date, a missing transport identification or a missing transport document reference.
claims.note: The only required-answer error proven on this page is the means of transport, and the only date rule is the allowed window.

claims.statement: The commodity selection page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/commodities.
The commodity selection page is headed, at level one, What are you importing?, which is also its overview task row's name.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'What are you importing?' });

claims.statement: The commodity selection page offers a box labelled Search for a commodity with a Search button, and lists nothing until the search is used: no checkboxes and no selected-commodities panel.
The commodity search is hinted "You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus)."
claims.quote: export const SEARCH_HINT = 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).';

claims.statement: The commodity selection page shows an inset reading "You must submit a separate notification for every single ITAHC. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an ITAHC."
claims.quote: 'You must submit a separate notification for every single ITAHC. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an ITAHC.',

claims.statement: The commodity selection page offers help titled Help with commodity codes which, when opened, shows a link named Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab) to https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff opening in a new tab.
A commodity search of fewer than three characters lists nothing.

Commodity search results are grouped by commodity code, the groups in ascending code order, and each group's species checkboxes in ascending species-label order; the results hold exactly the groups and species the reference-data service returns for that query.
claims.note: Proven for the queries 0102, cattle, horse, domestic cat and ostrich, each checked against the reference-data API's own answer.

claims.statement: A commodity group is named by its commodity name and then its code in brackets, such as Cattle (0102), and by the code alone when no name is held for it.
The text a trader searched for is shown in bold inside the commodity group's heading and inside the matching species label, including when the match falls inside the species' common name.
A commodity search that matches nothing shows No results found and lists no checkboxes.

Species found under different searches can be chosen together and are saved: reopening the page shows the chosen count, lists each species and shows each checkbox still checked when its search is run again.
The selected-commodities panel counts what has been chosen as "<n> selected", and a Clear all button empties it.

Saving the commodity selection page with nothing chosen is refused with Select a commodity, shown in the error summary and added to the search box's description as "Error: Select a commodity", and the summary link moves focus to the search box.
With search results already listed, the Select a commodity error still sits on the search box and the results stay on the page.

Clearing a saved commodity selection and pressing Save and return to overview is refused with Select a commodity, holds the trader on the page and leaves the selected-commodities panel gone, and the selection saved before is still there when the page is reopened.
claims.quote: test('keeps the saved selection when the page is reopened'

claims.statement: The selected-commodities panel heads each chosen commodity with its group name followed by a colon and lists one entry per chosen species, each with a control named Remove <latin name> from <group name>.
Removing one chosen species from the panel leaves the other chosen, and a save keeps only the one left.
Without JavaScript the commodity selection page's Remove and Clear all controls post the page and behave as they do with JavaScript.
claims.quote: test('removing one chosen species leaves the other selected and Clear all empties the panel, with every control posting the page'

claims.statement: The commodity selection page accepts a commoditySearch answer with action set to search, which answers with a page of results, and a species answer holding each chosen pair as its commodity code, a vertical bar and the species' Latin name.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the commodity pages' form bodies; shows that a search is a post to the same page and that a chosen species is identified by code and Latin name together.

claims.statement: The commodity lines the suite answers with are cattle 0102 Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle), bison 0102 Bison bison (American Bison), horse 0101 Equus cabalus (Horse), donkey 0101 Equus asinus (Donkey), domestic cat 01061900 Felis catus (Domestic Cat), raccoon dog 01061900 Nyctereutes procyonoides (Raccoon Dog), ostrich 01063300 Struthio spp. (Ostriches) and chicken 01051111 Gallus gallus (Chicken).
claims.quote: cattle: { searchTerm: 'Bos taurus', commodityCode: '0102', latinName: 'Bos taurus', commonName: 'Domestic Cattle' },
claims.note: Copied from the reference-data fixture, so it is evidence of what reference-data serves today rather than of what a notification must capture.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts the commodity search box's placeholder, nor the Search button's accessible name beyond the word Search, nor any limit on how many commodities may be chosen.
The Identification details page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/commodities/identification.
The Identification details page is headed, at level one, Identification details, which is also its overview task row's name.
The identifiers the Identification details page can ask for are Ear tag, Passport, Microchip, Horse name, Tattoo, Identification details and Description.
A cattle notification's Identification details page asks for an Ear tag and a Passport, and offers no Save and add another button when only one animal is expected: Save and continue is the only save.
The ear tag and the passport number are empty when the Identification details page opens.
An ear tag such as UK123456789012 is accepted with no error.

The Identification details page summarises the notification's commodities in a table with one row per commodity code, listing that code's species labels in that row and the total number of animals across them.
claims.note: Proven with two cattle-code species of two animals each summing to 4, and a cat on its own row showing 2.

claims.statement: Each species' identification card sits under a section headed by its commodity code, and the cards follow the order the species are listed for selection.
claims.quote:
await expect(pages.page.locator('main h2, main h3')).toHaveText([
      cattle.commodityCode,
      speciesLabel(bison),
      speciesLabel(cattle),
      domesticCat.commodityCode,
      speciesLabel(domesticCat),

await expect(animalsPages.animalIdentification.savedAnimalRow(commodityLines.cattle, 1)).toBeVisible();
    await expect(bisonBison.getByLabel('Ear tag', { exact: true })).toHaveValue('');

claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.animalIdentification.errorSummaryLinks).toHaveText(['Enter at least one identifier for this animal']);

claims.statement: Save and return to overview with every identifier blank saves no animal and shows no error.
Each species card is headed Enter details for <species label> <animal number> of <total animals>.

Pressing Enter in a card's identifier box saves that animal and keeps the trader on the Identification details page: the saved animal is listed with its identifier, the card's counter moves on to the next animal, and the box is cleared.
Pressing Enter after an animal is already saved appends a second row to that species' own table and leaves another species' table unchanged.
A saved animal is listed as a row named by its species label and its number, with a Remove control.

Pressing Save and continue leaves a species expecting more than one animal unsaved: Save and continue goes on to Additional details, and returning to Identification details shows that species back at its first animal with its box empty.

A Selected commodities row's Change link opens the commodity selection page with every species already chosen listed; adding one there and saving returns to Identification details with the added commodity in the summary.
Deselecting a species through a Change link returns to Identification details listing only the commodities left.
A species card's save control is labelled Save and add another while more animals are expected and Save and finish for the last one.
claims.quote: return card.getByRole('button', { name: SAVE_AND_ADD_ANOTHER }).or(card.getByRole('button', { name: SAVE_AND_FINISH }));
claims.note: Read from the card's save-control locator, which accepts either button, and from flows/animals/journey.ts:916-921, which presses Save and add another for the first of two animals and Save and finish for the second.

claims.statement: An ear tag of 59 characters is over the service's limit, so the limit is 58 characters.
claims.note: The constant's name says 59 is one over the limit; the spec uses it only to fill a sibling card that is never saved, so no test in this part proves the resulting error message.

claims.statement: The Identification details page accepts the answers animalIdentifierEarTag-<line index>, animalIdentifierPassport-<line index>, animalIdentifierMicrochip-<line index>, animalIdentifierTattoo-<line index>, identificationDetails-<line index> and description-<line index> when posted straight to it.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the Identification details page's form body from the notification's commodity lines, indexed by the line's position.

claims.statement: The identifiers each species needs differ: cattle answers an ear tag, a cat and a donkey and a horse a passport number, and an ostrich free-text identification details.
claims.quote: /** One animal per line, answering only what the frontend requires of that species. */
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's mandatory-answer set, built to satisfy what the frontend requires of each species today, not a statement of which identifiers the notification must capture.

claims.statement: A cat line also answers a permanent address, either the place of destination or a new address holding a name or organisation name, two address lines, a town or city, an optional county, a postcode, a phone number and an email address.
claims.quote: export type PermanentAddressAnswer = { origin: 'placeOfDestination' } | ({ origin: 'newAddress' } & NewPermanentAddressFields);
claims.note: The permanent address page itself belongs to part 2; this records only what the identification answers carry for it.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts that the Microchip, Horse name, Tattoo, Identification details or Description boxes are shown for any species, nor which identifier columns a saved-animals table holds.

claims.statement: The CPH number page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/cph-number.
The CPH number page is headed, at level one, Add the county parish holding number (CPH).
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH)' });

claims.statement: The CPH number is entered in three boxes labelled County, Parish and Holding number.
The CPH number is hinted For example 12/345/6789, with no full stop.

The CPH number page offers help titled What is a CPH number? which, when opened, shows a paragraph beginning "You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by" and a link named checking your holding details on GOV.UK to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number.
All three CPH boxes are empty when the page opens.
A CPH number of 12, 345 and 6789 saved with Save and continue takes the trader back to the Consignment addresses page, which shows the number as 12/345/6789.
Saving the CPH number page blank is accepted: the trader returns to Consignment addresses where the CPH number is still offered as something to add.
Typing all nine digits of a CPH number straight into the County box keeps every digit in that box and leaves focus there, and the number saves as 12/345/6789.
claims.note: No JavaScript moves focus between the three boxes as the trader types.

claims.statement: Without JavaScript, a whole CPH number typed with slashes into the County box is accepted and shown with its slashes on the Consignment addresses page.
The CPH number page is reached from the Consignment addresses page's add-CPH control.
The CPH number page accepts the answers cphCounty, cphParish and cphHolding when posted straight to it.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts any validation error on the CPH number boxes: no message for a part-filled number, a letter, or a number of the wrong length.
The Additional details page is addressed at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/additional-details.
The Additional details page is headed, at level one, Additional details, which is also its overview task row's name.
The Additional details page asks "What are the animals certified for?" as a group of radios, described by the hint You can find this information on the ITAHC.
The certification question offers Slaughter, Registered equine animal and Further keeping.
claims.note: Only Slaughter is asserted visible by a spec in this part; the other two are exercised by the journey walks.

claims.statement: The Additional details page asks "Does the consignment contain any unweaned animals?" as a group of Yes and No radios.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('group', { name: 'Does the consignment contain any unweaned animals?' });

claims.statement: The unweaned animals question is not shown for every consignment: the journey checks it is visible before answering it.

claims.statement: Nothing in this part asserts an error for leaving the certification question or the unweaned animals question unanswered, and no spec here asserts the whole option list of the certification question.
